lessons.title: TDS on Rent Above 50,000 Rupees a Month: What Tenants Must Do

body.text: Pay more than ₹50,000 a month in rent and the tax law turns you into a tax collector for your landlord. For a resident landlord it is a once-a-year job with no TAN needed. Ignore it and you pay interest and fees. Do it properly and you also get the strongest HRA evidence there is.

children.text: Premium rentals are common now: a 3BHK in Bandra, a flat in DLF Phase 5 in Gurugram, a gated community off Sarjapur Road in Bengaluru. Many salaried tenants paying these rents have never heard that they are required to deduct tax from it. Landlords rarely mention it, and employers do not handle it for you. This lesson covers what you must do, for both resident and NRI landlords.
Who Must Deduct TDS on Rent

markDefs.definition: Tax deducted at source by the tenant from rent paid to the landlord and deposited with the government in the landlord's name. The landlord gets credit for it against their own tax.

children.text: Under Section 393(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 194-IB of the 1961 Act), an individual or HUF paying rent to a resident landlord must deduct

body.caption: When a tenant must deduct TDS on rent

cells: You are an individual or HUF not required to deduct tax under the business provisions
Salaried employees and most individuals are covered. Businesses subject to tax audit follow a different rule
Rent exceeds ₹50,000 for a month or part of a month
Exactly ₹50,000 does not trigger it. ₹50,001 does
The landlord is resident in India
For NRI landlords, a stricter rule applies, covered below
The payment is rent for land, a building or both
A residential flat you live in is covered

body.label: The trigger
body.context: Applies to salaried tenants too. No TAN is needed. You use your PAN and file one challan-cum-statement, Form 141, for the year.

body.caption: TDS on rent paid to a resident landlord, tax year 2026-27

cells: Rate
2% of the rent if the landlord has a valid PAN linked to Aadhaar
Rate without a valid PAN
20%, but the TDS cannot exceed the rent for the last month of the year or tenancy
When to deduct
Once, from the rent for the last month of the tax year (March), or the month you vacate if earlier
How to deposit and report
Form 141, a PAN-based challan-cum-statement on the e-filing portal, which replaced Form 26QC
Deadline to deposit
Within 30 days from the end of the month in which you deducted the tax
Certificate to landlord
Form 132, which replaced Form 16C, within 15 days from the Form 141 due date

children.text: Aditi rents a 3BHK in Bandra West for ₹1,00,000 a month for the whole of tax year 2026-27. Her landlord has a valid PAN.

body.title: Aditi's TDS on rent for tax year 2026-27

events.title: Pay full rent
events.description: She pays ₹1,00,000 every month by bank transfer. No TDS yet.

events.title: Deduct TDS from the last rent
events.description: TDS is 2% of the year's rent of ₹12,00,000, which is ₹24,000. She pays the landlord ₹76,000 for March.

events.title: File Form 141 and pay
events.description: She deposits ₹24,000 through Form 141 using her PAN and her landlord's PAN.

events.title: Give Form 132 to the landlord
events.description: She downloads the TDS certificate from the portal and gives it to her landlord, who can see the credit in their AIS and Form 26AS.

body.title: Quick Check: Who Must Deduct?
body.question: Which of these tenants must deduct TDS on rent under Section 393(1)?
options: Farah pays exactly ₹50,000 a month to a resident landlord in Kolkata
Varun pays ₹65,000 a month to a resident landlord in Hyderabad and is a salaried employee
Priya pays ₹45,000 a month to a resident landlord in Chennai
Sunil pays ₹48,000 a month in rent and ₹1,500 in separately billed society charges directly to the society
body.explanation: Only Varun's rent exceeds ₹50,000 a month. Farah is at exactly ₹50,000, which does not exceed the limit. Priya is below it. Sunil's society charges are paid to the society, not as rent to the landlord, so his rent stays at ₹48,000. Being salaried does not exempt Varun.

body.title: Try It: Meera Moves Out in January
body.prompt: Meera pays ₹75,000 a month to a resident landlord with a valid PAN in Pune from April 2026 and vacates at the end of January 2027. How much TDS must she deduct, and from which month? Enter the TDS amount in rupees.
body.explanation: She paid rent for 10 months, April to January, totalling ₹7,50,000. TDS at 2% is ₹15,000, deducted from her January rent because that is the last month of her tenancy. Her Form 141 is due within 30 days of the end of January, by 2 March 2027.

children.text: When Your Landlord Is an NRI

If your landlord is a non-resident, for example working in Dubai or the US and renting out a flat in Bengaluru, the rules are much stricter. Tax is deducted under Section 393(2) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (Section 195 of the 1961 Act).

columns.label: Resident landlord
points: Only if rent exceeds ₹50,000 a month
2% rate with valid PAN
Deduct once a year
No TAN needed, Form 141 with your PAN
Certificate: Form 132

columns.label: NRI landlord
points: Applies to any amount of rent, with no threshold
30% plus 4% cess, and surcharge if applicable, unless a lower deduction certificate or treaty rate applies
Deduct from every payment
TAN required, quarterly TDS statement in Form 144, which replaced Form 27Q
Certificate: Form 131, which replaced Form 16A

body.text: Budget 2026 removed the need for a TAN when a resident individual buys property from an NRI, from 1 October 2026. That relief is for property purchases. It does not cover rent paid to an NRI landlord, so tenants still need a TAN and must file quarterly statements.

body.title: Scenario: The Landlord in Dubai
body.scenario: Rohit, a software engineer, rents a flat in Whitefield for ₹40,000 a month. The owner moved to Dubai two years ago and asks Rohit to keep paying the full rent into her NRO account "as before". Rohit claims HRA on ₹4,80,000 of rent a year.
body.prompt: What obligations has Rohit missed, what are the risks, and what should he do?
body.modelAnswer: His landlord is a non-resident, so every rent payment attracts TDS under Section 393(2), whatever the amount. At 30% plus 4% cess, that is about ₹12,480 a month. Rohit needs a TAN, must deduct and deposit TDS each month, file quarterly statements in Form 144 and issue Form 131 certificates. If he does not, he can be treated as a defaulter for the tax he failed to deduct, with interest and fees. The ₹50,000 threshold for resident landlords does not help him. He should apply for a TAN, speak to the landlord about deductions going forward, and suggest she obtain a lower deduction certificate if her actual tax liability is lower. For past months, he should take a chartered accountant's advice on regularising the default. His HRA claim remains based on the gross rent of ₹40,000 a month, since the TDS is part of the rent paid on the landlord's behalf.

children.text: TDS on rent is a separate obligation from your HRA claim, but the two support each other. Form 141 records your PAN, your landlord's PAN and the rent paid, and the TDS appears in your landlord's AIS and Form 26AS. That is independent, government-held proof that you paid rent to that landlord. For HRA, use the gross rent before TDS, since the tax you deducted was paid on your landlord's behalf.

body.text: Missing TDS on rent is costly: interest of 1% a month for not deducting on time and 1.5% a month for deducting but not depositing, plus a late fee under Section 427 for filing Form 141 late. It can also create friction with your landlord, who cannot claim credit for tax that was never deposited. A calendar reminder for March, or the month you move out, avoids all of it.

body.title: TDS on Rent Checklist
steps: Check whether your monthly rent exceeds ₹50,000, and whether your landlord is resident or NRI
Collect and verify your landlord's PAN, and confirm it is linked to Aadhaar
Resident landlord: set a reminder for March, or the month you plan to vacate, to deduct 2% of the year's rent
File Form 141 and pay the TDS within 30 days from the end of that month
Download Form 132 and give it to your landlord within 15 days of the Form 141 due date
NRI landlord: get a TAN before the first payment, deduct from every payment, file Form 144 quarterly and issue Form 131
Keep the Form 141 acknowledgement with your HRA evidence file

cards.definition: Requires individuals and HUFs paying a resident landlord more than ₹50,000 a month to deduct 2% TDS once a year. Replaced Section 194-IB.
PAN-based challan-cum-statement for depositing and reporting TDS on rent. Replaced Form 26QC. Due within 30 days of the end of the month of deduction.
TDS certificate given to the landlord for TDS on rent. Replaced Form 16C. Due within 15 days of the Form 141 due date.
TDS on payments to non-residents, including rent to NRI landlords, at 30% plus cess with no threshold. Replaced Section 195.
The quarterly TDS statement for payments to non-residents (replacing Form 27Q) and the non-salary TDS certificate (replacing Form 16A).

points: If you pay a resident landlord more than ₹50,000 a month, you must deduct TDS on rent under Section 393(1), even as a salaried employee
Deduct 2% of the year's rent once, from March rent or your last month's rent, and deposit it through Form 141 within 30 days
Without the landlord's valid PAN, the rate is 20%, capped at the last month's rent
Give your landlord Form 132 within 15 days of the Form 141 due date
For an NRI landlord, deduct 30% plus cess from every payment, with a TAN, quarterly Form 144 and Form 131 certificates
Form 141 is strong HRA evidence, and your HRA claim uses the gross rent before TDS

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or financial advice. TDS provisions, forms and due dates reflect the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026 as understood at the time of writing. Rent to non-residents can involve treaty and certificate issues. Verify current rules or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
